parsed.explanation: Thin-data territory. No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented targeting, arrests, facility restrictions, or police hostility appears in the record — no traveller-facing exposure is documented. Decriminalisation came by external court order (2001) and the sodomy issue is tangential to trans visitors. Positive signals are dated (2012/2017: among the more welcoming islands in the region) and sexuality-specific, describing conservative undercurrents ('silent and invisible', secret gay life) rather than documented trans acceptance. Open questions — unsettled marriage recognition and unclear extension of the governing state's equality protections — are unanswered questions, not exposures, so they hold the score down only modestly. Extrapolating from no criminalisation, no documented harms, a dated warmth signal, and conservative social undertones in a functioning small-territory system: elevated-to-reduced risk, around the 0.65 tier, with residual uncertainty from thin trans-specific evidence in either direction.
